Subject: Quartzline SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant log retention and deletion evidence

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The security team is preparing a SIG/CAIQ return and we have two focused asks relating to retention/deletion for our assessment:

1) Tenant-scoped inference logs: what is the default retention for request/response logs and the per-tenant debug traces? Can you provide the deletion workflow (who/what triggers deletion, TTL enforcement, and sample proof of deletion)?

2) Customer-specific exceptions: Quartzline needs a documented process for requesting and approving an extended retention window for a small set of tenants (up to 180 days) for ongoing fraud investigations. What controls, approval flows, and compensating controls does Redwood apply when granting such exceptions?

We attached a short spreadsheet with the SIG questions we want answered inline (attachment: quartzline_sig_questions.xlsx). Ideally we'd receive a consolidated response and any artifacts (SOC 2 mapping, retention matrix, sample proof-of-delete) by next Thursday 11/26 to hit our internal audit milestone.

Appreciate your help — feel free to loop in product/legal if needed.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Head of Security, Quartzline

Subject: Re: Quartzline SIG/CAIQ follow-up — tenant log retention and deletion evidence

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet.

Short answers up front:
- Default retention: request/response generation logs are retained 30 days by default; ephemeral debug traces are retained 7 days.
- Exception process: we support documented, timeboxed exceptions (up to 180 days) on a per-tenant basis with an approval workflow that requires Product, Security, and Legal sign-off plus compensating access controls (IP allowlist + scoped auditor role).

I've attached a retention matrix and our SOC 2 mapping for the relevant controls (retention_matrix_vs_soc2.pdf). We can provide a sample proof-of-delete (s3 object deletion record + internal deletion job run log) — I'll pull a sanitized example for you.

A couple of clarifying questions before we draft the official response:
- Will Quartzline require the extended window for all tenants under your org or only a small subset (please indicate estimated number of tenants)?
- Do you need audit-proof attestation (signed letter / DocuSign) or will a console-delivered evidence bundle (Drive link + hash) suffice for your SIG/CAIQ reviewers?

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm scope (# of tenants and whether PII is involved).
2) We draft an exception request template and share the approval flow.
3) We deliver artifacts (retention matrix, SOC2 crosswalk, sample proof-of-delete) by 11/26.

I'll start gathering the deletion logs and the sample artifacts; cc'ing Karthik (infra lead) and Ben (security) to confirm the runbook and approval template.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Grace / Ben — quick internal note that I'll prepare a sanitized proof-of-delete from the deletion-job logs and include the S3 lifecycle event IDs + job run metadata. A few implementation details for the exception flow:

- Approval gates: Product review (impact to modeling/rollouts), Security risk sign-off (Ben), Legal attestation (we'll need Legal to approve contract amendment language)
- Compensating controls: tenant-level encryption keys (customer KMS allowed on Dedicated/Private only), restricted auditor role (read-only, time-limited), daily integrity snapshots hashed and stored in an immutable bucket for 365 days (forbucket)
- Automation: exception entries are recorded in our ticketing system and create an immutable audit record (ticket id + approver ids + expiry timestamp).

Ben — can you confirm the security sign-off template and whether a signed attestation (DocuSign) is required in addition to the console evidence?

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
